subject: Final sizing request + temporary fleet slot reserve for TidalAI pilot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Chen <sophie@tidalai.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Final sizing request + temporary fleet slot reserve for TidalAI pilot

Hi Ben / Karthik,

TidalAI (Sophie cc'd) is greenlighting a 6-week pilot starting roughly the week of Sep 8. They've given us their production-like profile (attached), and the buyer is asking if we can hold standby capacity while procurement finishes the PO.

Key ask: can we place a short-term soft hold for a pool equivalent to ~8 A100-80GB GPUs (they're estimating ~300 concurrent tokens/sec with 32k context on the model they're testing) starting Sep 8 and covering the pilot ramp (6 weeks)? If exact hardware mapping isn't possible, a capacity-equivalent hold (same TFLOPS/KV capacity) is ok.

This will be a late-stage deal; we should avoid committing dedicated pods permanently until procurement completes, but Sophie is insistent we block capacity so customer doesn't walk. Please confirm:
- Inventory availability for Sep 8–Oct 20 window
- Proposed hold type (soft hold / provisional earmark / reserved node) and maximum hold time we can offer without an MSA/signature
- Ops constraints: can we allow burst autoscale above the hold if needed, or should we cap at the reserved envelope?
- Any suggested alternatives (e.g., quantized model variant / mixed instance packing) to reduce the footprint while keeping latency targets.

I've attached the inference profile and a draft SLA Sophie asked us to review.

Thanks,
Marissa
Head of Strategic Deals | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0192

Attachments: tidalai-inference-profile.csv, proposed-sla-draft-2025.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Chen <sophie@tidalai.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Final sizing request + temporary fleet slot reserve for TidalAI pilot

Marissa — thanks for the detail and the profile. Quick inventory/status:
- Usable pool: dedicated-us-west-2-pool-b currently has 42x A100-80GB slots free as of this morning.
- Thermal/placement notes: we can earmark a group that will meet the KV-cache and sequence-length needs without fragmentation.

Recommendation for a short-term hold:
- Offer a "soft hold" (provisional earmark) for the equivalent of 8x A100-80GB GPU capacity for 21 calendar days. During that window we can extend once if procurement has proof-of-progress (PO-in-flight).
- Hold semantics: the nodes remain available for workload routing but are flagged as "provisionally allocated" — they will not be fully provisioned (no charge) until the PO is executed. This avoids permanent customer billing while giving a functional reservation.
- Autoscale: we can permit controlled burst up to 2x the hold (policy-based) if cluster free capacity exists, but bursts will be on a best-effort preemptible basis. Suggest we include that in the customer messaging.

Operational items I need from Sales/Product:
- Confirmation of the model variant (float16 vs 4-bit quantized) — that will materially affect node counts.
- Expected p95 latency SLO and token-rate ramp (daily).

I'll attach a short ops note on how we'll implement the soft hold and the internal ticket I'll open.

— Ben
Ben Carter | Capacity & Sales Ops
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachment: ops-soft-hold-playbook (internal)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Chen <sophie@tidalai.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Aug 2025 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Final sizing request + temporary fleet slot reserve for TidalAI pilot

Looping in a quick sizing note. After parsing the profile (thanks Marissa), baseline assumptions:
- Model: LLM-32k ~ 90B-ish, expected steady-state ~300 tok/s, p95 latency target 250–350ms
- If we serve float16 across A100-80GB: ~8 GPUs recommended for headroom (matches ask).
- If customer accepts 4-bit quantized variant we can likely compress to 5–6 GPUs equivalent with slight p95 lift.

Pricing/commit implications: soft hold for 21 days is fine. If procurement needs a longer soft hold (beyond 21 days) we should ask for a nominal commitment (e.g., refundable reservation fee or a non-binding LOI) — ops won't block inventory >45 days without a ticket escalation.

Operational caveats:
- We need engineering sign-off on KV-cache sizing with that model variant; I'll ping runtime eng to run a quick bench with their profile (should be 24–48h).
- If the customer requires steady autoscale above the held envelope we must convert to a short-term reserved pod (billable) to guarantee capacity.

I'll open OPS ticket OPS-9271 and request the bench. I'll attach a short note outlining the quantization tradeoffs we discussed internally.

Karthik
Head of Field Engineering | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Attachment: quantization-recommendation-notes.md

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Chen <sophie@tidalai.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Final sizing request + temporary fleet slot reserve for TidalAI pilot

Thanks both — this is perfect. Sophie, per our internal check we can offer a provisional soft hold for the equivalent of 8 A100-80GB GPUs in our us-west-2 pool starting Sep 8, with a 21-calendar-day soft-hold window. We will permit controlled burst auto-scale up to 2x on a best-effort basis if spare capacity exists, but sustained burst requires conversion to a short-term reserved pod (billable).

Next steps for TidalAI:
1) Sophie — please confirm whether your team is open to testing a 4-bit quantized variant during the pilot. If yes, we may be able to reduce the operational footprint to 5–6 GPUs (improves headroom and reduces chance of contention).
2) Sophie — share PO-in-flight confirmation (email to procurement@redwood.ai) once submitted so we can extend the soft hold if needed.
3) Ben / Karthik — please create OPS-9271 and run the bench on the attached profile. If we get clear results, we will lock the soft hold and notify Sophie by EOD Aug 22.

Sophie — happy to jump on a 20-minute call if you want to walk the SLA and hold semantics before the PO.

Best,
Marissa
